summary: A list stores several values in order under one name. You get each value by its index, starting at 0.
notes: scores[0] is the first value. scores[len(scores) - 1] is the last.
scores[2] = 79 replaces the value at index 2.
append() adds a value to the end, and len() grows by 1.
pitfall: Using an index equal to len(scores) causes IndexError: list index out of range. The last index is len(scores) - 1.
